meta.description: Test whether two or more traits share a causal variant at a locus using Bayesian colocalization (coloc.abf, coloc.susie, HyPrColoc, moloc, eCAVIAR, SMR/HEIDI, PWCoCo, SharePro). Use when integrating GWAS with eQTL/sQTL/pQTL/mQTL, distinguishing shared causal variants from LD-driven coincidence, handling allelic heterogeneity, choosing between single-causal vs multi-causal methods, picking PP.H4 thresholds, running sensitivity over p12, or harmonising summary statistics for colocalization.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 test datasets are explicitly labelled synthetic/planted-truth; no fabricated DOI/PMID, trial results, sample sizes, or p-values presented as real. SKILL.md's own 15 literature citations (Giambartolomei 2014, Wallace 2020/2021, Zhu 2016, Hormozdiari 2016, Foley 2021, Mountjoy 2021, Vosa 2021, etc.) were spot-checked and are real, correctly attributed papers.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-genomics / statistical-genetics research tooling only; no output makes an individual diagnostic or prescriptive claim. Not applicable to patient care by design; no disclaimer gap found.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found (correlation-vs-causation distinctions, e.g. SMR-vs-coloc reconciliation, are handled correctly). One real precision issue -- the 'PP.H3 inflation at r2 0.3-0.6' trigger condition is overstated relative to empirical testing (see Input 3, P1 recommendation) -- is a documentation-accuracy gap, not a fallacy: no output inverts a causal conclusion or substitutes correlation for causation.

code_usability.detail: Core method code (coloc.abf across 5 tested scenarios, coloc.susie once given self-consistent data, the SMR CLI flag set) runs correctly with real, checkable output. Two of the Skill's five shipped example files (examples/coloc_susie.R, examples/coloc_susie_multicausal.R) crash unconditionally and reproducibly on this installed coloc 5.2.3 / susieR 0.14.2 -- but the failure is a runtime numerical error from internally-inconsistent synthetic demo data (LD matrix generated independently of the simulated betas), not a syntax error, infinite loop, or missing dependency, so it does not meet this gate's literal FAIL trigger. Elevated to a P0 recommendation instead (see recommendations) because it is a 100%-reproducible failure of the Skill's reference implementation for one of its two central documented methods.

functional_suitability.note: Very broad, accurate coverage of 8 methods with a clear decision tree (4/4 completeness, 4/4 appropriateness). Correctness docked to 2/4: the two shipped coloc.susie example files crash unconditionally (verified independently, see run/skill_own_example_check.txt and run/skill_own_example2_check.txt), and the PP.H3-inflation trigger condition (r2 0.3-0.6) is empirically overstated (Input 3).

reliability.note: Category-3 override applied: the extensive Common Errors table (10 rows, each with cause+solution), explicit hard-stop diagnostics (estimate_s_rss lambda>0.05 -> stop), and precise error-text matching are exemplary defensive design for an agent-first analysis skill.

performance_context.note: Linear, non-redundant workflow (4/4 execution efficiency). SKILL.md itself is 460 lines with no references/ folder to defer detail into -- token cost scored 3/4 for the monolithic structure, though the information density is legitimately high given 8-method breadth.

agent_usability.note: Clear one-liner method summaries, consistent PP.H0-H4/p12/sdY/s terminology throughout, explicit output-format guidance (Reviewer-Grade Reporting Template, 10 points), and unusually thorough proactive error-prevention guidance (sdY mismatch flagged as 'most common silent failure', s-parameter footguns, LD-order silent-failure warning).

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md Quick Start / Example Prompts are natural-language and highly discoverable (verified against Inputs 1-7, all phrased in that style and correctly triggered the right section). Frontmatter description itself is jargon-dense (method-name list) rather than natural phrasing -- discoverability scored 3/4. Forgiveness scored 4/4 under the Category-3 override (strict validation is a documented feature, not a defect).

security.note: No credentials anywhere in this domain; extensive input validation (allele harmonisation, flip/palindromic-SNP logic, LD row/column order checks) is a genuine strength; no sensitive-data handling since inputs are non-identifiable summary statistics.

maintainability.note: Sections are clearly delineated by method/topic (4/4 modifiability). Modularity scored 3/4 -- SKILL.md carries taxonomy + decision tree + failure modes + priors + thresholds + all pipelines in one file with no references/ split. Testability scored 2/4: example scripts are seeded and in principle reproducible, but 2 of the 5 shipped examples do not run at all (see functional_suitability note), directly undermining 'outputs are deterministic and verifiable' for that subset.

agent_specific.note: Precise, comprehensive trigger description (4/4) and unusually strong composability -- 13 explicitly cross-referenced Related Skills with clear input/output boundaries, verified plausible against the causal-genomics workflow (4/4). Deterministic/idempotent given fixed data and seed (4/4). Progressive disclosure scored 3/4 (see performance_context). Escape hatches scored 3/4: the underpowered-eQTL (N<200) and MHC/chr8-inversion exclusion rules are clearly documented in prose, but unlike the LD-mismatch check there is no runnable coordinate-range guard for MHC/inversion exclusion (verified gap, Input 6).

key_strengths: The coloc.abf pipeline (harmonise -> format -> run -> sensitivity) runs out-of-the-box and reproduces planted-truth PP.H4/PP.H3 exactly across every tested scenario (single-causal, distinct-causal, multi-tissue, MHC) -- 5 of 5 coloc.abf-based inputs completed cleanly.

Failure-mode documentation is unusually specific and mostly verified accurate: the Common Errors table, sdY/s semantics warnings, and the estimate_s_rss LD-mismatch diagnostic (lambda>0.05) all held up under direct testing, correctly catching the Skill's own documented SNP-order silent-failure mode.

Extensive, accurate cross-referencing to 13 related Skills with clear input/output boundaries (e.g. coloc-validated SNPs feeding causal-genomics/mendelian-randomization) supports real end-to-end workflow composability.

Threshold and prior guidance (PP.H4 bands, p12 sensitivity grid, palindromic-SNP handling) is well-sourced to primary literature (Giambartolomei 2014, Wallace 2020/2021, Zhu 2016) and internally consistent across SKILL.md and usage-guide.md.

recommendations.title: Both shipped coloc.susie example files crash unconditionally
recommendations.problem: examples/coloc_susie.R and examples/coloc_susie_multicausal.R -- the Skill's only two worked demonstrations of its second central method -- both terminate with a runtime error ('the estimated prior variance is unreasonably large' / a documented-diagnostic stop()) on the installed coloc 5.2.3 / susieR 0.14.2, verified by running both files unmodified. This is not a version-drift issue (both packages match the Skill's stated minimum versions).
recommendations.root_cause: Both files build a toy exponential-decay LD matrix independently of the simulated per-SNP betas/SEs, so the LD is not internally consistent with any genotype process that could have produced those z-scores; estimate_s_rss correctly detects this (lambda 0.21-0.39, far above the Skill's own 0.05 threshold).
recommendations.fix: Regenerate both example datasets from a single simulated genotype matrix, deriving both the GWAS/eQTL summary statistics AND the LD matrix from that same genotype matrix (verified working in this audit's run/input2b_susie_selfconsistent.R, which recovers the planted 2-credible-set truth exactly with lambda=0).

recommendations.title: PP.H3-inflation trigger condition (r2 0.3-0.6) is overstated
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'coloc.abf -- PP.H3 inflation under multiple causal variants' section states that 2 causal variants in moderate LD (r2 ~0.3-0.6) 'forces' the model to inflate PP.H3; a well-powered simulation at r2=0.513 (shared-eQTL / allelic-heterogeneity configuration) instead resolved cleanly to PP.H4=1.0.
recommendations.root_cause: The real trigger for this failure mode depends jointly on LD, relative effect sizes, and statistical power, not on r2 alone; the documentation presents only the r2 condition as if it were sufficient.
recommendations.fix: Qualify the trigger condition with its power/effect-size dependency, or add a concrete worked example showing the specific effect-size ratio and power regime under which PP.H3 actually inflates.

recommendations.title: MHC exclusion is enforced only by prose, with no programmatic gate
recommendations.problem: Unlike the LD-mismatch check (estimate_s_rss lambda>0.05, an explicit runnable gate), the MHC/chr8-inversion exclusion relies entirely on the agent noticing the coordinate range and applying judgment; none of the Skill's worked code patterns check chr/position against the documented exclusion windows.
recommendations.root_cause: No coordinate-range guard was included alongside the other pipelines' worked code, unlike the LD-consistency check which does have one.
recommendations.fix: Add a short guard snippet (chr==6 && 25e6<=pos<=35e6, or chr==8 && 8.1e6<=pos<=11.9e6) to the Standard coloc.abf Pipeline code block that emits the required caveat automatically before printing PP.H4, mirroring the estimate_s_rss stop() pattern already used for LD mismatch.

recommendations.title: SMR + HEIDI recipe never numerically exercised in this audit
recommendations.problem: No real GTEx/eQTLGen BESD + matched plink bfile pair was available in this environment; only the CLI flag set was verified against the real SMR 1.3.1 binary, not the full pipeline's numeric output (SMR p / HEIDI p / nsnp_HEIDI).
recommendations.root_cause: BESD reference panels are large (100MB-1GB+) and building one from scratch was out of scope for a single audit input in this session.
recommendations.fix: Cache a small chromosome-scoped BESD + matching plink bfile subset (e.g. one GTEx tissue, one chromosome) in the shared audit environment so a future pass can numerically verify the SMR/HEIDI half of this Skill's central operation.

recommendations.title: Frontmatter description is jargon-dense relative to natural user phrasing
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description lists method names (coloc.abf, HyPrColoc, eCAVIAR, PWCoCo, SharePro) that a domain novice is unlikely to type verbatim, while usage-guide.md's own Quick Start examples are far more natural and were what actually matched Inputs 1-7's phrasing.
recommendations.root_cause: The description appears optimized for agent-facing keyword-trigger precision rather than human discoverability.
recommendations.fix: Fold 1-2 of usage-guide.md's natural-language Quick Start phrasings directly into the frontmatter description.

recommendations.title: HyPrColoc cross-tissue clustering not verified this session
recommendations.problem: hyprcoloc was not yet installed in the shared audit environment when Input 5 ran; the multi-tissue decision-tree branch's cross-tissue clustering half was scored by inspection only.
recommendations.root_cause: Environment tooling for this candidate (coloc, susieR, hyprcoloc, SMR) was still being extended in parallel with this audit run.
recommendations.fix: Re-run the HyPrColoc half of Input 5 once hyprcoloc lands in the shared environment; expect a Tissue1/Tissue2 cluster given the per-tissue effect sizes planted in run/input5_multitissue.R.
